gen-dafont-quantum-gf-noto-sans-zanabaza: Noto Sans Zanabazar Square is a friendly plain sans with a soaring x-height and wide gaps that keep tiny sizes crisp. Quantum, a display face, draws every stroke without taper, so enlarge the body text a notch and it will hold its own.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-noto-traditional-n: Crisp, techy, and wide open. Quantum runs uninterrupted monoline strokes up top, while Noto Traditional Nushu follows with a broad-nibbed pen stroke whose bowls fill the line, giving the pair a lively human-versus-machine tension.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-numans: Clean is the first impression: Quantum holds one constant stroke from top to baseline, with generous space between its letters. And Numans answers in sans-serif, with s shapes whose ends hang far from the spine and tracking pushed well past normal.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-onest: Onest reads with short ascenders perched above big bowls, and its line thickness stays gently uniform throughout. Quantum, the display heading, sits above with loose spacing, and the whole page moves along smoothly without a single snag.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-open-sans: Open Sans brings bulky lowercase proportions and a smooth read with no clogged curves, so text feels sturdy. Quantum is better at hairline-free display work, tight and techy.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-orienta: Orienta has counters that breathe like a hollow reed cut open, with little height difference between its cases. Quantum above it keeps curves at the heft of a rope's body, and Orienta softens that with its modern, quiet sans-serif voice.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-oxygen: Quantum's ruler-straight line weight looks crisp and technical, and Oxygen follows with curves that never close back on themselves. Its lowercase nearly matches the capitals.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-parkinsans: Modern and bright. Parkinsans keeps one stroke thickness everywhere, with wide-mouthed letters that stay crisp when shrunk, so a long passage under Quantum's loose, clean heading moves along without friction.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-pathway-extreme: Quantum draws its heading like spaghetti laid out in letters, loose and techy with a compressed ascender length. But Pathway Extreme, a plain sans, brings stubby ascenders and descenders beside a big x-height, and clear openings in every round letter.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-preahvihear: Preahvihear opens each letter mouth like a pried oyster shell and lifts a lofty x-height above the line. And Quantum keeps its thickness steady around every curve, so the heading and body feel tidy and modern together.
